title: Duplicate embeddings generated when re-ingesting the same repository
body: The `pipeline.py` doesn't check whether a repo has already been ingested before processing it. Re-uploading the same GitHub repo generates duplicate vector entries, causing retrieval to return identical chunks with inflated scores.

title: Add support for ingesting a portfolio website URL
body: Allow users to submit a URL to their personal portfolio site. The pipeline should fetch the page content, extract relevant text (bio, project descriptions), and include it in the vector store alongside GitHub and resume data.

title: Add a content hash to detect unchanged documents and skip re-embedding
body: When a user re-submits the same README without changes, the pipeline should detect that the content hash hasn't changed and skip the embedding step, reducing unnecessary API calls.

title: Add support for parsing GitHub Actions workflow files to detect CI/CD skills
body: Developers who maintain CI/CD workflows demonstrate DevOps skills that don't appear in `import` statements or README text. Add a parser that reads `.github/workflows/*.yml` files and extracts inferred skills (e.g., `GitHub Actions`, `Docker`, `pytest`, `deployment`).

title: Add end-to-end ingestion test with a sample resume fixture
body: `ingestion/pipeline.py` has no test coverage. `ResumeParser`, `ReadmeParser`, and `BatchEmbeddingProcessor` have unit tests under `tests/unit/`, but no test runs `IngestionPipeline.ingest_resume` through parsing, chunking, and embedding storage, and `tests/integration/` holds only an empty `__init__.py`. Add an integration test that builds an `IngestionPipeline` with stub objects for `vector_db`, `db_session`, and `embedding_provider`, loads a resume from `tests/fixtures/sample_resumes/`, passes it to `ingest_resume`, and asserts on the `chunk_count` of the returned `IngestResult`.

title: Hybrid retriever over-weights keyword results when query contains technology names
body:
`HybridRetriever.retrieve` blends vector and keyword scores with a default weighting of 0.7 for vector and 0.3 for keyword, and nothing else in the repo sets different weights.

`retrieve` fetches the collection's chunks with `_get_all_chunks` and then discards the result instead of passing it to `keyword_searcher.index()`, so the BM25 index is never built from the profile's own chunks. `KeywordSearcher.search` returns an empty list until `index` has run, so the keyword half of the blend adds nothing.

The score normalization is the second problem. `retrieve` divides the scores on each side by the highest score in that side's own batch of results, so the best BM25 hit always becomes 1.0 no matter how low its raw score is. Once the chunks are indexed, a chunk that is the best keyword match only because it repeats a technology name such as "React" or "Python" takes the full 0.3 keyword contribution, which is exactly the default `min_score` of 0.3, and `retrieve` keeps any result at or above that threshold even when its vector score is 0.

Pass the fetched chunks to `keyword_searcher.index()`, and normalize keyword scores against a fixed scale rather than the batch maximum, so a weak keyword match does not pass the `min_score` filter on its own.

title: Vector store returns stale embeddings after a document is re-ingested
body: When a README is updated and re-ingested, the old embeddings remain in the vector store alongside the new ones. The retriever can return outdated chunks that don't reflect the current document content.

title: Review generator never combines feedback across a user's projects
body:
The review generator never combines observations across a user's projects. `ReviewGenerator._consolidate_feedback` is the only step meant to do that, and it merges nothing: it keeps the first section for each `section_name` and drops any later section whose `section_name` it has already seen. When parsing succeeds, `generate_section` returns the first section from the parsed model output, so the `section_name` it carries comes from that output and not from the requested section name. Nothing else in `rag/generator/` combines feedback.

There is also no per-project detail for the model to work with. `generate_full_review` calls `generate_section` once for each of five fixed section names (`skills_feedback`, `projects_feedback`, `presentation_feedback`, `gaps_feedback`, `first_impression`), so the number of sections does not depend on the number of projects. `generate_section` fills its template with three values: the formatted context, `github_username`, and `project_count`, which is `len(profile_data.get("projects", []))`. All five templates in `rag/generator/prompt_templates.py` use those same three placeholders, so nothing else from `profile_data`, including the project entries themselves, reaches the model.

Pass per-project detail into the prompts, and give `_consolidate_feedback` a real implementation that merges repeated observations into a single statement covering the projects it applies to.

title: Implement a caching layer for repeated identical portfolio queries
body: When a user submits the same portfolio for review twice without making changes, the system re-runs the full RAG pipeline. Add a cache keyed on the profile's content hash that returns the stored review if the portfolio hasn't changed.

title: Implement a re-ranking step that uses an LLM to score retrieved chunks before generation
body: The current retriever uses vector + keyword scores for ranking. Add an optional re-ranking pass that prompts a smaller LLM to score each retrieved chunk's relevance to the query before passing the top-k to the generator.

title: Architecture doc doesn't explain the hybrid retrieval scoring formula
body: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` describes that hybrid retrieval blends vector and keyword scores but doesn't explain the formula or the default weights. Add a section explaining the scoring logic with an example.

title: Add snapshot tests for prompt templates to catch accidental changes
body: Prompt templates directly affect review quality. Add snapshot tests that fail if a template's content changes without a version bump, so developers must consciously version templates rather than silently editing them.

title: Add an integration test that runs the full RAG pipeline against a mock LLM
body: The RAG components have unit tests (`tests/unit/test_keyword_search.py`, `tests/unit/test_relevance_scorer.py`, `tests/unit/test_output_parser.py`), but `tests/integration/` holds only an empty `__init__.py`, so no test runs a full query through retrieval → generation → parsing. Add one that indexes a small set of chunks, calls `HybridRetriever.retrieve` with a query embedding from `MockEmbeddingProvider`, passes the chunks it returns to `ReviewGenerator.generate_full_review`, and asserts on the returned `FeedbackSection` objects, which `generate_section` builds by passing the model output through `parse_review_output`. `ReviewGenerator.__init__` builds its own `openai.OpenAI` client and the repo has no fake generation client, so the test has to supply a client of its own that returns a fixed response. Mark the test `@pytest.mark.integration` so `make test-integration` runs it, and build the profile argument from the fixture in `tests/fixtures/sample_profiles/`.

title: Implement an offline eval runner that measures review quality across a benchmark portfolio set
body:
`scripts/run_evals.py` is a stub: `main()` prints two lines and returns (`scripts/run_evals.py:4-12`). The scoring code it needs already exists — `EvalSuite.run(query, chunks, feedback)` in `rag/evaluator/eval_suite.py:30` returns an `EvalResult` with `relevance_score`, `faithfulness_score` and `overall_score` — but nothing in the repo calls `EvalSuite`, so review quality is never measured. The rest of the setup is already in place: `make eval` runs `scripts/run_evals.py` (`Makefile:77-78`), and the RAG Evaluation workflow runs `python scripts/run_evals.py` (`.github/workflows/eval.yml:21`) and then reads `eval_results.json` to report the scores (`.github/workflows/eval.yml:32`). When the workflow cannot comment on the pull request, it writes the scores into the job summary instead (`.github/workflows/eval.yml:38-48`).

Implement the runner so it loads the benchmark profiles from `tests/fixtures/sample_profiles/`, runs each one through retrieval and generation, scores the result with `EvalSuite`, and writes `eval_results.json` with per-profile scores and an overall score for the whole set. The workflow runs it with `LLM_PROVIDER: mock` set (`.github/workflows/eval.yml:23`), so the runner must finish without a real API key: use `MockEmbeddingProvider` from `ingestion/embeddings/provider.py` for embeddings and a fake client for the generator.

title: Agent session state is not cleared between reviews for the same user
body:
`SessionStore` keys agent state on the `session_id` it is passed, and `Orchestrator.run` passes the profile id as that id. Nothing reads the state it loads to decide what to skip: the state is only merged with the new results and written back, and `SessionStore.delete` is never called, so entries from earlier reviews stay until the one hour expiry that `SessionStore.set` applies.

The results a second review reuses come from the in-memory cache in `ContextManager`. Each `Orchestrator` holds one `ContextManager`, `_execute_tool` returns the stored result whenever a tool name and the hash of its input repeat, and `ContextManager` has no method that removes entries, so one `Orchestrator` serving two reviews returns the first run's result for every tool whose input is unchanged.

Clear the `ContextManager` cache at the start of `Orchestrator.run`, and delete the profile's stored state with `SessionStore.delete` before the plan runs, so a review that follows a portfolio update runs the tools again.

title: Orchestrator catches all exceptions from tool calls and continues without logging the failure
body: The plan-execute loop wraps each tool call in a broad `except Exception` that silently continues. When a tool fails, the orchestrator produces a review with missing sections and no indication to the user that something went wrong.

title: Agent state isn't persisted across API restarts, causing in-progress reviews to be lost
body: Long-running reviews (5+ repositories) that span a server restart lose their progress. The in-flight session state is held only in memory and not written to Redis until completion.

title: Add a `has_tests` boolean to the repo analysis output
body:
`RepoAnalyzer` in `ingestion/parsers/repo_analyzer.py` already detects tests. `_detect_tests()` looks for `tests/`, `test/`, `pytest.ini`, `test_`, `__tests__`, and `spec/`, and its result becomes the `has_tests` key in the parser metadata and the `Has Tests:` line in the summary text. The problem is the input. `_detect_tests()` reads those names from `repo_data.get("file_structure", "")`, and no code in this repository ever sets `file_structure`, so `has_tests` is always `False`. `_detect_ci()` and `_detect_tech_stack()` read the same key, so `has_ci` is always `False` and `tech_stack` holds at most the primary language.

`RepoAnalyzer.parse()` expects the raw GitHub API response for a repository: it reads `stargazers_count`, `forks_count`, `pushed_at`, `language`, `readme_content`, and `html_url`. `GitHubTool._fetch_repo_metadata()` in `agent/tools/github_tool.py` fetches that API response, but it returns its own dict with different names — `star_count`, `fork_count`, `last_commit_date`, `primary_language`, `has_readme`, plus `name`, `description`, `open_issues_count`, `topics`, and `homepage` — and it has no file list. Nothing in the repository passes one of these dicts to the other. `RepoAnalyzer.parse()` is called only from `ingest_repo_metadata()` in `ingestion/pipeline.py`, which receives `repo_data` from its caller.

The work is to give the detectors a file list. Two pieces are needed: add a method to `GitHubTool` that lists the files in the repository, and make the dict that reaches `RepoAnalyzer.parse()` carry that list under a `file_structure` key. `_has_readme()` in `agent/tools/github_tool.py` already makes a second GitHub API request, so use the same pattern for the new request. The three detectors wrap the value in `str()`, so a list of paths works.

title: Add a `contribution_streak` field to the GitHub analysis (longest consecutive days of commits)
body: Consistent contribution activity is a portfolio signal. Add a tool that computes the user's longest consecutive commit streak from their GitHub contribution history.

title: Implement a `DependencyAuditTool` that flags outdated major dependencies in project repos
body: Add a new tool that parses `requirements.txt`, `package.json`, or `pyproject.toml` files in submitted repos and flags dependencies that are more than one major version behind the current release.

title: Add a plan validation step that checks tool prerequisites before executing the plan
body: The orchestrator executes tools without checking their dependencies. For example, the skill extractor depends on ingestion being complete, and the market analyzer depends on the tech detector having run first. Add a DAG-based plan validator.

title: Add a mock GitHub API server for integration tests
body:
`tests/integration/` holds only an `__init__.py`, and no test in the repository exercises `GitHubTool`. The `test-integration` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `pytest tests/integration` and treats pytest's "no tests collected" exit code as success, so the tool's request building and its error handling are not checked anywhere.

Add integration tests that run `GitHubTool` against a local mock server instead of the live GitHub API. `pytest-httpserver` is already in the `dev` dependency group in `pyproject.toml`, and `GitHubTool` sets `self.base_url` in `__init__()` and builds every request URL from it, so a test can point the tool at the mock server's address. Cover a successful metadata fetch plus the 404 and 403 responses that `execute()` turns into "Repository not found" and "Rate limited or access denied". Keep the JSON response bodies as fixture files in `tests/fixtures/github_responses/`. Once the directory collects at least one test, remove the exit code shim from the `test-integration` job, as the comment there asks.

title: Add an end-to-end agent test using a fully stubbed tool suite
body: There is no test that exercises the full agent lifecycle (plan → execute → synthesize) without live dependencies. Add an integration test using stub implementations of all tools and the mock LLM.

title: Prompt injection defense doesn't sanitize newline characters in user-supplied resume text
body:
Adversarial users can inject newline sequences into their resume text that terminate the system prompt and append new instructions. The sanitizer strips `<`, `>`, and `{` but misses `
---
` and `
System:` patterns.

title: Safety monitoring doesn't emit metrics when the content filter is bypassed by a multi-turn conversation
body: The monitoring system logs safety events for single-turn requests but doesn't track cases where a user circumvents the content filter across multiple API calls. Add cross-request pattern detection for known bypass sequences.

title: Add a safety event count to the health check endpoint
body:
The `/health` endpoint in `api/routes/health.py` returns a `safety_events_last_hour` key whose value is the literal `0`. It is set to `0` where `health_status` is built and assigned `0` again after the dependency checks, and the route never reads the safety layer, so the number never changes.

`SafetyMonitor` in `safety/monitoring.py` records events with `log_event()`, which increments one Redis key per event type, and reads them back with `get_event_count()`. Create a `SafetyMonitor` with a Redis client in the route and fill the field from the counts for the five types in `SafetyMonitor.VALID_EVENT_TYPES`. If the counts cannot be read, keep the current behavior: log the error and leave the field at `0` rather than failing the health check. `get_event_count()` ignores its `window_hours` argument and returns the raw Redis counter, which `log_event()` gives a 24 hour expiry, so the field reports that counter total rather than a strict one hour window.

title: Add a "feedback tone check" that ensures all generated feedback is written constructively
body: After generation, add a tone classification step that uses a prompt to classify whether each feedback section is constructive (actionable, specific, encouraging) or negative (discouraging, vague, dismissive). Reject and regenerate sections that fail.

title: Add rate limiting per IP address in addition to per user
body:
`RateLimiter.check_rate_limit` in `safety/rate_limiter.py` takes any identifier string — its docstring names a user ID or an IP address, and `tests/unit/test_rate_limiter.py` covers a user ID, an IP address, and an API key. Nothing in `api/` calls it. `api/main.py` adds only `CORSMiddleware` and `RequestIDMiddleware`, and no route or dependency builds a `RateLimiter`, so no request is limited today, authenticated or not.

Add middleware in `api/middleware/`, registered in `api/main.py`, that calls the limiter on every request: once with the client IP address as the identifier, and once with the user ID when the request carries a token that `decode_access_token` in `core/security.py` accepts. Build the Redis client from `redis_url` in `core/config.py`, read the limit from `rate_limit_per_minute` in the same file, and return `429 Too Many Requests` when a check fails. `api/middleware/request_id.py` shows the middleware pattern this app uses.

title: Implement a red-teaming test suite for the prompt injection defense
body: Add an automated test suite that attempts a curated set of known prompt injection attacks against the safety layer and verifies that all are blocked. This suite should run in CI on every PR that touches `safety/`.

title: Add a bias audit report that runs over a sample of stored reviews
body: Implement an offline bias audit script (`scripts/audit_bias.py`) that samples 100 stored reviews, runs them through the bias detector with detailed logging, and produces a report showing false positive/negative rates by demographic signal.

title: Add integration tests for the full safety middleware chain
body: Unit tests exist for individual safety components but there's no test that runs a request through the full safety stack (prompt defense → content filter → bias detector → PII scrubber). Add an integration test with fixtures covering pass and fail cases for each layer.

title: `DELETE /profiles/{profile_id}` leaves the profile's embeddings in the vector store
body:
`DELETE /profiles/{profile_id}` in `api/routes/profiles.py` calls `delete_profile` in `core/services/profile_service.py`. That function deletes the profile's `Review` rows and `IngestedSource` rows, then the profile, and commits once, rolling back if anything fails. The models declare the same cascade: `core/models/profile.py` sets `cascade="all, delete-orphan"` on the `reviews` and `ingested_sources` relationships, and `core/models/review.py` and `core/models/ingested_source.py` both set `ondelete="CASCADE"` on `profile_id`. No database rows are left behind.

The vector store is not cleaned up. `ingestion/pipeline.py` puts `profile_id` and a `source_id` such as `resume_{profile_id}_{hash}` into the metadata of every chunk it stores in ChromaDB, and `VectorStore.delete_by_source_id` in `rag/retriever/vector_store.py` has no callers, so the chunks for a deleted profile stay in the store and retrieval can still return them.

Delete a profile's chunks from the vector store as part of `delete_profile`. `delete_by_source_id` shows the pattern to follow: select the chunks by metadata, then delete the IDs it returns. Nothing outside `rag/retriever/` holds a `VectorStore` today, so the service needs one passed in, and the route that calls the service has to supply it.

title: Concurrent review requests for the same profile can produce inconsistent results
body: If a user submits two review requests simultaneously, both requests start the agent loop against the same profile state. The second agent loop may read stale data modified by the first. Add a per-profile lock to serialize concurrent reviews.

title: Add an API rate limiting header (`X-RateLimit-Remaining`) to responses
body:
`RateLimiter.check_rate_limit` in `safety/rate_limiter.py` returns an allow or deny result plus the number of requests left in the current window, but nothing in `api/` calls it: `api/main.py` registers only `CORSMiddleware` and `RequestIDMiddleware`. The API never counts a request, never returns `429`, and sends no `X-RateLimit-Limit` or `X-RateLimit-Remaining` header.

Add a middleware in `api/middleware/` and register it in `api/main.py`. It should call `check_rate_limit` once per request, using a Redis client built from `redis_url` in `core/config.py` and `rate_limit_per_minute` from the same file as the limit. Set `X-RateLimit-Limit` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining` on the response from that limit and the returned count, and return `429` when the call denies the request. `api/middleware/request_id.py` shows the pattern: it sets `X-Request-ID` on the response inside its `dispatch` method.

title: Implement a webhook system that notifies users when their review is ready
body: Long-running reviews (multiple repositories) can take 30–90 seconds. Add a webhook endpoint where clients can register a callback URL that receives a `POST` with the review payload when processing is complete.

title: `POST /reviews` endpoint has no test for when the profile has no ingested documents
body: There's no test that exercises the review endpoint when a profile exists but has no associated ingested content. Add a test that verifies the endpoint returns an appropriate error rather than crashing.

title: API reference doc is missing the `POST /profiles` request body schema
body:
`docs/API.md` lists endpoints one per line with a short description and documents no request bodies. Add the request body for `POST /profiles` and `POST /reviews`, with a description and an example value for every field.

`POST /profiles` takes multipart form data rather than JSON: `create_profile_endpoint` in `api/routes/profiles.py` declares `github_username` and `portfolio_url` as `Form` fields and `resume_file` as a `File` upload. `POST /reviews` takes a JSON body validated by `ReviewCreate` in `api/schemas/review.py`, which has one field, `profile_id`.

title: Add integration tests for authentication edge cases
body:
`api/middleware/auth.py` has no test coverage. `tests/integration/` holds only an empty `__init__.py`, and `tests/conftest.py` defines only the `sample_resume_text` and `sample_readme_text` fixtures, so no test sends a request to the API. `tests/unit/test_security.py` covers `decode_access_token` with an invalid token, a malformed token, and a token with a changed payload, but `get_current_user` is never called.

Add `tests/integration/test_auth_middleware.py` with tests that call a protected endpoint such as `GET /reviews` and check the response for an expired token, a malformed token, a missing `Authorization` header, and a token signed with a different secret. This needs a client fixture built on the `app` in `api/main.py`; `httpx` is already a project dependency. None of the four cases reaches the user lookup in `get_current_user`, so the tests do not need a user row in the database. Mark the tests with the `integration` marker declared in `pyproject.toml`.

title: Review progress indicator doesn't update in real time during long-running reviews
body:
While a review runs, `frontend/src/pages/ReviewPage.tsx` renders a fixed spinner with the text "Analyzing your portfolio...", so a long review gives no sign of how far along it is and looks like the app has stopped responding. `frontend/src/hooks/useReviewStatus.ts` polls `GET /reviews/{id}/status` every 3 seconds through `apiClient.getReviewStatus`, and `get_review_status` in `api/routes/reviews.py` returns a `progress_pct` field.

Replace the spinner with a progress bar driven by that field. `progress_pct` is always 0 today: `core/models/review.py` has no `progress_pct` column, the route reads it with `getattr(review, "progress_pct", 0)`, and the `Review` type in `frontend/src/types/index.ts` has no such field. The work covers recording progress on the review while `process_review` runs, carrying the field through to the client, and rendering it.

title: Add a "Copy link" button to share a public review summary
body: Allow users to generate a shareable link to a read-only view of their review summary. The link should be accessible without login and expire after 30 days.

title: Add a before/after comparison view for users who have completed multiple reviews
body: Users who review their portfolio at two different points in time have no way to see how their scores changed. Add a comparison view that shows side-by-side diffs of two selected reviews.

title: Add accessibility tests for the review page using `jest-axe`
body: The review page has no automated accessibility checks. Add `jest-axe` tests that verify the page doesn't have common accessibility violations (contrast, missing labels, improper heading structure).

title: Test coverage for `core/services/review_service.py` is below 40%
body: The review service orchestrates the full review workflow and is the most critical service in the application, but most of its code paths are untested. Add unit tests targeting the major execution paths including success, partial failure, and full failure cases.

title: No property-based tests for the PII scrubber
body: The PII scrubber handles an enormous variety of personal data formats. Add property-based tests using `hypothesis` to generate randomized PII inputs and verify the scrubber always removes them.

title: Add a performance benchmark for the ingestion pipeline to detect regressions
body: Large portfolio ingestion (5 repos + resume) should complete within 30 seconds. Add a benchmark test using `pytest-benchmark` that fails if mean ingestion time exceeds the threshold.

title: API docs don't include example `curl` commands
body: `docs/API.md` describes each endpoint but has no example invocations. Developers setting up the project for the first time can't quickly verify the API is working.

title: Add inline docstrings to all public methods in `core/services/`
body:
Every public function in `core/services/` already has a docstring, but none of them has the `Args:`, `Returns:` or `Raises:` sections that Google style asks for. Add the sections that apply to each of the eight public functions, and keep the text each docstring already has.

`core/services/profile_service.py` defines `create_profile`, `get_profile`, `update_profile` and `delete_profile`. `core/services/review_service.py` defines `create_review`, `get_review`, `list_reviews` and `process_review`. Only two of the eight catch errors, and they behave differently, so the docstrings should describe what the code really does: `delete_profile` rolls back the transaction and re-raises when the cascade delete fails, so it needs a `Raises:` section, while `process_review` logs `review_processing_failed`, sets the review status to `failed`, and returns without raising, so it does not.

title: Write a contributor onboarding guide that walks through a complete issue → PR lifecycle
body: New contributors need a walkthrough that takes them from forking the repo to getting a PR merged. Cover: setting up the dev environment, running tests, finding and understanding an issue, making a change, and passing CI.

title: Add a dependency vulnerability scan to the CI pipeline
body: The project has no automated check for known security vulnerabilities in its Python or JavaScript dependencies. Add a step that runs `pip audit` and `npm audit` and fails the build on high-severity findings.

title: Add a database migration validation step to CI that checks all migrations can be applied cleanly
body: Schema migrations are tested manually before merging but not in CI. Add a step that spins up a fresh database, runs all migrations in order, and verifies the schema matches the SQLAlchemy models.

title: PII scrubber fails to redact parenthesized US phone numbers
body:
The phone-number pattern in `pii_scrubber.py` matches dashed formats like `555-123-4567` but not the parenthesized format `(555) 123-4567`, so one of the most common US phone formats passes through `scrub()` unredacted, and `detect()` reports no PII for it.

**Steps to reproduce:**
```python
from safety.pii_scrubber import PIIScrubber
s = PIIScrubber()
print(s.scrub('Call me at (555) 123-4567 or 555-123-4567'))
# observed: 'Call me at (555) 123-4567 or [REDACTED]'
print(s.detect('Call me at (555) 123-4567'))
# observed: []
```
Related failing tests: `test_us_phone_number_redaction`, `test_us_phone_formats`, `test_detect_phone_pii`, `test_phone_at_start_of_text` in `tests/unit/test_pii_scrubber.py`.

title: Resume section detection fails on text with leading whitespace
body:
`_detect_sections()` in `resume_parser.py` anchors every section-header pattern at the start of a line (`^Experience`, `\nExperience`). Text extracted from PDFs commonly preserves leading indentation, and for such input no sections are detected at all — `detected_sections` comes back empty.

**Steps to reproduce:**
```python
from ingestion.parsers.resume_parser import ResumeParser
r = ResumeParser()
res = r.parse('\n    John Smith\n    john@example.com\n\n    Education:\n    - B.S. Computer Science\n\n    Skills: Python\n')
print(res.metadata['detected_sections'])
# observed: []  (expected: Education, Skills)
```
Related failing tests: `test_parse_single_column_resume_text`, `test_parse_resume_no_work_experience`, `test_detect_sections` in `tests/unit/test_resume_parser.py`.

title: Skill extractor fails to detect JavaScript and TypeScript
body:
`_detect_languages` in `ingestion/parsers/skill_extractor.py` looks for `.js` and `.ts` only in the `filename` argument (lines 175 and 177), and line 186 also picks `TypeScript` over `JavaScript` from the filename alone, so `TypeScript` is never reported when no filename is passed. The block reads just two signals from `text`: `re.search(r"\b(import|require)\s+", text)` on line 179 and the literal `package.json` on line 181. Text that describes JavaScript or TypeScript work in any other way produces no `JavaScript` or `TypeScript` language entry. `extract_skills('Wrote index.js using const arrow functions and async/await callbacks')` returns an empty list, and `extract_skills('Built app.tsx and types.ts with strict TypeScript interfaces')` returns only `React`, which comes from the `.tsx` entry in `REACT_INDICATORS` on line 55. Make the block read these signals from `text` as well: file names the text mentions, the keywords already listed in `JS_TS_KEYWORDS`, and the words JavaScript and TypeScript.

`_detect_tools` and `_detect_databases` have the same problem: each one matches a technology only when its own name appears in the text (`if tool in text_lower` on line 268, `if db in text_lower` on line 253). Dockerfile directives, a Compose file, and `import psycopg2` never contain the words `docker` or `postgresql`, so `test_devops_tool_detection` gets `['Python']`, `test_docker_compose_detection` gets `[]`, and `test_database_technology_detection` gets `['Python', 'JavaScript']`, where that `JavaScript` entry comes from `import psycopg2` matching the line 179 regex. Add signals for those patterns too, such as the `FROM`/`RUN`/`EXPOSE` directives and a `services:` block for Docker, and the `psycopg2` driver name for PostgreSQL.

Five tests in `tests/unit/test_skill_extractor.py` are marked `@pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True)` against this issue and should pass once all three detectors read the text: `test_javascript_detection`, `test_text_with_typescript_files`, `test_devops_tool_detection`, `test_docker_compose_detection` and `test_database_technology_detection`. Remove the markers as part of the fix.

**Steps to reproduce:** `pytest tests/unit/test_skill_extractor.py -q` — observed: the five tests above fail their assertions and report as `xfailed`, with `test_javascript_detection` getting `[]` and `test_text_with_typescript_files` getting `['Python']` where each expects a JavaScript or TypeScript entry.

title: Structural chunker silently drops documents that contain no headings
body:
`StructuralChunker.chunk()` returns an empty list for any document without markdown headings, so the entire document is silently excluded from the RAG index instead of being chunked as a single block or falling back to another strategy.

**Steps to reproduce:**
```python
from ingestion.chunking.structural_chunker import StructuralChunker
c = StructuralChunker()
print(len(c.chunk('This is a plain document with no headings at all. ' * 20, {})))
# observed: 0  (a ~1000-char document produces no chunks)
```
Related failing test: `test_document_with_no_headings` in `tests/unit/test_structural_chunker.py`.

title: Tech detector counts vendored and build-output files, skewing language detection
body:
`tech_detector.py` does not exclude `node_modules/` or `build/` paths. A repo with 2 Python source files and 6 vendored/bundled JS files is reported as primarily JavaScript.

**Steps to reproduce:**
```python
from agent.tools.tech_detector import TechDetector
t = TechDetector()
files = ['main.py','core/app.py','node_modules/lib/index.js','node_modules/lib/util.js','node_modules/x/a.js','node_modules/y/b.js','build/bundle.js','build/vendor.js']
print(t.execute({'files': files}).data['primary_language'])
# observed: 'JavaScript'  (expected: 'Python')
```
Related failing tests: `test_node_modules_excluded`, `test_build_directory_excluded` in `tests/unit/test_tech_detector.py`.

title: Bias detector patterns are too narrow to match common phrasings
body:
The regex patterns in `bias_detector.py` require near-exact phrase sequences (e.g. “bootcamp graduates lack rigor”) and miss natural phrasings of the same bias, such as “The candidate only attended a bootcamp, so this project lacks the rigor of a formal CS education” or age-based assumptions like “Given their age, they likely cannot keep up with modern frameworks”. Nine unit tests specifying the intended coverage fail.

**Steps to reproduce:**
```python
from safety.bias_detector import BiasDetector
print(BiasDetector.detect_bias('The candidate only attended a bootcamp, so this project lacks the rigor of a formal CS education'))
# observed: (False, '')  (expected: flagged as dismissive educational-background language)
```
Related failing tests: 9 tests in `tests/unit/test_bias_detector.py` (e.g. `test_dismissive_bootcamp_language_detected`, `test_demographic_assumption_age_detected`).

title: Faithfulness checker can never mark short claims as supported
body:
`_is_supported()` requires at least 2 non-stopword tokens to overlap between a claim and the context. Short factual claims (e.g. “The candidate knows Python.”) share only one meaningful token with a fully supporting context, so they are always scored unsupported — feedback consisting of short, fully supported claims scores 0.0.

**Steps to reproduce:**
```python
from rag.evaluator.faithfulness_checker import FaithfulnessChecker
f = FaithfulnessChecker()
print(f.check('Knows Python. Knows SQL.', [{'text': 'python expert'}, {'text': 'sql expert'}]))
# observed: 0.0  (both claims are supported by the context)
```
Related failing tests: `test_partial_support_returns_middle_score`, `test_multiple_context_chunks`, `test_multiple_claims_varying_support` in `tests/unit/test_faithfulness_checker.py`.

title: Faithfulness checker crashes when a context chunk has `text: None`
body:
`check()` builds the context with `chunk.get("text", "")`, but when the key is present with value `None`, `.get()` returns `None` (the default applies only to missing keys), and the subsequent `" ".join(...)` raises `TypeError`.

**Steps to reproduce:**
```python
from rag.evaluator.faithfulness_checker import FaithfulnessChecker
FaithfulnessChecker().check('Knows Python.', [{'text': None}])
# observed: TypeError: sequence item 0: expected str instance, NoneType found
```
Related failing test: `test_none_context_chunk_text` in `tests/unit/test_faithfulness_checker.py`.

title: Health check DB probe passes a raw SQL string, which fails under SQLAlchemy 2.x
body:
The database probe in `api/routes/health.py` executes the literal string "SELECT 1". SQLAlchemy 2.x requires textual SQL to be wrapped in `sqlalchemy.text()`, so the probe raises and the health check reports the database as down even when it is reachable.

**Steps to reproduce:** call `GET /health` with the stack running (or invoke the route handler in a unit test with a live session) and observe the database check failing with `ArgumentError: Textual SQL expression 'SELECT 1' should be explicitly declared as text('SELECT 1')`.

title: Health check references `settings.redis_host`, which does not exist on Settings
body:
The Redis probe in `api/routes/health.py` builds its client from `settings.redis_host` and `settings.redis_port` (lines 47 and 48). `Settings` in `core/config.py` defines neither field; it carries a single `redis_url` (line 14), which is also the only Redis variable in `.env.example`. The resulting `AttributeError` is raised inside the probe's `try` block and caught by the `except Exception` on line 55, so the caller never sees that error. Instead the handler logs `redis_health_check_failed`, sets `dependencies.redis` and the top-level `status` to `"unhealthy"`, and then raises `HTTPException` with status 503 on lines 86-89, carrying the whole health dict as the detail. Redis reports as down on every call, even when it is reachable.

Point the probe at `settings.redis_url`, which `redis.Redis.from_url()` accepts directly. Both lines need the change: fixing only `redis_host` leaves the same failure one line later at `redis_port`.

**Steps to reproduce:** start the stack with Redis running and call `GET /health` — observed: a 503 whose body reports `"redis": "unhealthy"`, with `redis_health_check_failed` and an `AttributeError` for `redis_host` in the log; `grep redis_host core/config.py` confirms the field is absent from `Settings`.

title: README scorer test fixture is too short for its own word-count assertion
body:
`test_readme_with_all_quality_signals` asserts `data["word_count"] > 100` and `word_count_category == "comprehensive"`, but its fixture README contains only ~51 words, so the test fails against correct scorer behavior. Extend the fixture (or correct the assertion) so the test validates what it intends to.

**Steps to reproduce:** `pytest tests/unit/test_readme_scorer.py -q` — observed: `assert 51 > 100` fails.

title: Relevance scorer “partial overlap” test fixture actually has full query overlap
body:
`test_query_with_partial_overlap` uses query “Python Django web framework” against a chunk containing all four query terms, then asserts the score is below 0.9. The scorer correctly returns 1.0 for full keyword coverage, so the test fails against correct behavior. Fix the fixture so the overlap is genuinely partial.

**Steps to reproduce:** `pytest tests/unit/test_relevance_scorer.py -q` — observed: `assert 1.0 < 0.9` fails.

title: review_service unit tests misconfigure async mocks — 13 of 19 tests fail
body:
The service code correctly awaits `db.execute(...)`, but the tests build their mock session so that `result.scalars()` returns a coroutine, causing `AttributeError: 'coroutine' object has no attribute 'first'` (and `'all'`) inside otherwise-correct service code. Rework the mock setup (e.g. `AsyncMock` for `execute`, `MagicMock` for the result object) so the existing CRUD tests actually run.

**Steps to reproduce:** `pytest tests/unit/test_review_service.py -q` — observed: 13 failed, 6 passed.

title: structlog output is not captured by pytest caplog — log assertions fail suite-wide
body:
The application logs through structlog, which is not configured to propagate into the stdlib logging system during tests. Every test asserting on `caplog` (e.g. `test_empty_chunks_list_returns_empty` in `tests/unit/test_batch_processor.py`) fails even though the code under test does emit the expected log event. Configure structlog in `tests/conftest.py` (e.g. via `structlog.stdlib` processors or `capture_logs`) so caplog-based assertions work.

**Steps to reproduce:** `pytest tests/unit/test_batch_processor.py::TestBatchEmbeddingProcessor::test_empty_chunks_list_returns_empty -q` — observed: assertion on caplog fails while the warning is visibly printed to stderr.

title: Review creation does not verify profile ownership
body:
## Problem

The `POST /reviews` endpoint passes the authenticated user's ID to `create_review()`, but `core/services/review_service.py` ignores that argument when creating a review.

The service creates a `Review` from the supplied `profile_id` without checking that the profile belongs to the current user. This is inconsistent with `get_review()` and `list_reviews()`, which already scope review reads through `Profile.user_id`.

## Impact

An authenticated user who knows another user's profile UUID may be able to create a review for that profile by sending:

```text
POST /reviews
{"profile_id": "<another-users-profile-id>"}

title: Keyword search raises `ZeroDivisionError` when the index is empty
body:
`KeywordSearcher.index()` builds the BM25 index at `rag/retriever/keyword_search.py:25` by passing the tokenized corpus to `BM25Okapi`. When the chunk list is empty the corpus is empty too, and rank-bm25 divides the total token count by the number of documents to get the average document length, so `index([])` raises `ZeroDivisionError`. `search()` already handles the empty case with the guard at `rag/retriever/keyword_search.py:38` and returns an empty list, so `index()` should accept an empty corpus without raising and a search after it should return an empty list.

The covering test, `test_empty_index` in `tests/unit/test_keyword_search.py`, calls `searcher.index([])` before it searches. It is marked `@pytest.mark.xfail` referencing manifest id H-01 — remove the marker as part of the fix.

title: Output parser crashes on a top-level JSON array fallback
body:
When the LLM returns a top-level JSON array instead of an object, `output_parser.py` calls `.items()` on the parsed value and raises `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'items'`. The fallback path should handle array responses.

The covering test is marked `@pytest.mark.xfail` referencing manifest id H-02 — remove the marker as part of the fix.

title: README parser test fixture is indented, so it contains no headings
body:
`test_parse_standard_readme` in `tests/unit/test_readme_parser.py` parses the `sample_readme_text` fixture at `tests/conftest.py:26` and asserts `result.metadata["heading_count"] > 0`. Every line of that fixture that has text on it is indented by four spaces, and four-space indented text in Markdown is a code block rather than a heading, so `_extract_heading_hierarchy` finds nothing, the heading count is `0`, and the test fails against correct parser behavior. The parser is right: its heading pattern at `ingestion/parsers/readme_parser.py:55` matches the `#` and `##` headings in this repository's own `README.md`. Fix the fixture so its lines are not indented; without the indentation it contains three headings and the test passes.

The covering test is marked `@pytest.mark.xfail` referencing manifest id H-03 — remove the marker as part of the fix.

title: Heading hierarchy test fixture is indented, so it contains no headings
body:
`test_extract_heading_hierarchy` in `tests/unit/test_readme_parser.py` builds its markdown in a triple-quoted string whose lines are indented by eight spaces, then asserts that heading levels 1, 2 and 3 all appear. `_extract_heading_hierarchy` in `ingestion/parsers/readme_parser.py` matches `#` only at the start of a line, which is the correct rule: text indented by four or more spaces is a code block in Markdown, not a heading. The method therefore returns an empty list, and the test fails against correct parser behavior. This is the same fixture problem as issue #70 (manifest H-03). With the indentation removed, the same markdown gives four headings, at levels 1, 2, 3 and 2, which satisfies every assertion. Fix the fixture so its lines are not indented.

The covering test is marked `@pytest.mark.xfail` referencing manifest id H-04 — remove the marker as part of the fix.

title: `verify_password` raises `UnknownHashError` on malformed stored hashes instead of returning False
body:
`core/security.py` lets passlib's `UnknownHashError` escape when the stored hash is not a recognizable format. Verification against a malformed hash should fail closed (return `False`), not raise.

The covering test is marked `@pytest.mark.xfail` referencing manifest id H-05 — remove the marker as part of the fix.
